title: Plant Kingdom
seo_title: Plant Kingdom Class 11 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 3)
standard_text: Classification of plants into major groups; salient and distinguishing features and a few examples of algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes and gymnosperms.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 3 Plant Kingdom: algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms, their features, examples and life cycles. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Bryophytes: gametophyte dominant; pteridophytes onwards: sporophyte dominant.
body_html:
How to think about it

Algae are simple, mostly aquatic plants: green (Chlorophyceae), brown (Phaeophyceae) and red (Rhodophyceae). Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts) are the amphibians of plants with a dominant gametophyte. Pteridophytes (ferns, horsetails) are the first plants with xylem and phloem and a dominant sporophyte.

Gymnosperms (Pinus, Cycas) bear naked seeds; angiosperms bear seeds inside fruits and show double fertilisation, forming a triploid endosperm. Heterospory in Selaginella was a step towards the seed habit.

Example

Funaria is a?

moss

Answer: bryophyte

Example

Endosperm ploidy in angiosperms?

two polar nuclei + one male gamete

Answer: 3n

Common mistakes

  • Calling the fern plant a gametophyte.
  • Saying gymnosperms have fruits.
  • Mixing up brown and red algae pigments.

faq.q: Why are bryophytes called the amphibians of the plant kingdom?
faq.a: They live on land but need water for their sperm to swim to the egg.
In angiosperms one male gamete fuses with the egg and the other with the two polar nuclei, forming the zygote and the triploid endosperm.
